questions.question: If taxi fares increase and people immediately look for other transport options, the demand is considered to be:
options: Elastic
Inelastic
Unitary
Perfectly rigid

questions.question: Which phrase best describes an inelastic reaction?
options: People run away fast when the price goes up.
People stand there and take the price increase.
People find a cheaper substitute immediately.
People stop buying the product entirely.

questions.question: What is the primary relationship that elasticity looks at?
options: How price reacts to a change in demand.
How quantity demanded reacts to a change in price.
How supply reacts to a change in demand.
How consumers react to a change in income.

questions.question: What is the formal CAPS definition of Price Elasticity of Demand?
options: The responsiveness of price to a change in quantity demanded.
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price.
The percentage change in income divided by price.
The relationship between two different products.

questions.question: According to the Law of Demand, what happens when price increases?
options: Quantity demanded goes up.
Quantity demanded goes down.
Quantity demanded stays the same.
Supply goes down.

questions.question: Why do business owners care about price elasticity?
options: It tells them how sensitive customers are to price changes.
It helps them calculate their taxes.
It guarantees they will make a profit.
It determines the quality of their product.

questions.question: What is the correct formula for calculating Price Elasticity of Demand?
options: PED = % Δ P / % Δ Qd
PED = % Δ Qd / % Δ P
PED = Δ P / Δ Qd
PED = Qd / P

questions.question: In the elasticity formula, why is quantity demanded on top?
options: Because quantity is the cause and price is the reaction.
Because quantity is the reaction and price is the cause.
Because quantity is always a bigger number than price.
Because the textbook randomly decided it.

questions.question: How do you calculate the percentage change for price?
options: (Change in price / New price) * 100
(Change in price / Original price) * 100
(Original price / Change in price) * 100
(New price / Original price) * 100

questions.question: If price rises from R20 to R25, what is the percentage change in price?
If quantity demanded falls from 200 to 180, what is the percentage change in quantity demanded?
If the % Δ Qd is 15% and the % Δ P is 30%, what is the Price Elasticity of Demand?
If the Price Elasticity of Demand is calculated as 1.5, how is it classified?
options: Price Inelastic
Unitary Elastic
Price Elastic
Perfectly Inelastic

questions.question: If a product is classified as Price Inelastic, what does this mean about the customers?
options: They are very sensitive to price changes.
They will buy a different product immediately.
They are not very sensitive to price changes.
They only buy the product when it is on sale.

questions.question: What is an example of a product that usually has price inelastic demand?
options: Different brands of cold drink
Luxury sports cars
Basic necessities like bread
Movie tickets

questions.question: When PED is exactly 1, it is called Unitary Elasticity. What does this mean?
options: Percentage change in quantity is greater than percentage change in price.
Percentage change in quantity is less than percentage change in price.
Percentage change in quantity is exactly equal to percentage change in price.
The price did not change at all.
